inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt directs production actions on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation, which removes a natural check on ambiguous or mistaken requests.
The design relies on instruction text rather than an external confirmation or approval mechanism for sensitive production actions.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can reach the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions under the engineer identity
Chat transcript stores the request and rationale
Tamper resistant action provenance that binds request, agent action, and acting identity
Separate agent service identity instead of acting only under the engineer personal token

findings.title: Shared human identity and deletable transcript break attributable provenance for production actions

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start, so production actions are attributed in the cloud audit log to the human engineer rather than to a distinct agent identity.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

The prompt instructs the agent to deploy or run migrations in production when asked and to avoid confirmation, increasing the need for reliable attribution because the agent may act directly on terse requests.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so unattributable actions can have severe operational consequence.

recommendations.action: Issue the agent a distinct service identity and bind each production action to both the requesting engineer and the agent execution record.
Store tamper evident provenance linking the authenticated request, exact action, tool arguments, and outcome in a record the engineer cannot delete.

forecast.watch_signal: Raise a reassessment if chat retention is shortened, deletion remains user controlled, unattended steps increase, or the agent begins executing longer multi step production changes under the same shared human identity.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts say engineer access is SSO authenticated, but they do not describe session binding or any peer authentication details for the agent process itself.
No runtime or configuration artifact describes whether the agent prompt, deployment logic, or session token handling can be modified after release.
The described design has no egress capability and no external content source; the agent acts only on internal production systems from trusted engineer requests.
The artifacts do not state any step limit, runtime limit, or concurrency limit, so denial of service resilience of the process cannot be determined.
The agent uses the requesting engineer's own delegated credential rather than a broader shared service credential, so no broader authority than the principal is evidenced here.
The artifacts do not describe transcript access controls, retention scope, or whether other engineers can read another engineer's session history.
No evidence states retention quotas, availability protections, or whether deletion can remove records needed for operational investigation.
The notes say production actions are recorded, but they do not state whether the cloud audit log is immutable or protected from alteration by platform administrators.
The artifacts do not describe who can read the cloud audit log or whether log payloads include sensitive deployment or migration details.
No evidence covers log retention guarantees, pipeline capacity, or whether logging failures could suppress records during incident periods.

rating.rationale: The main evidenced risk is a present repudiation property failure: production actions are executed under the engineer's personal token while the only action-to-request linkage is a user-deletable transcript. No declared control restores attributable provenance, so residual remains high. Forecast does not rise above present because the design already lacks the key provenance control; reassessment is still required if autonomy or task horizon increases.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, IaC, or detailed runtime configuration was provided, so tamper resistance, log immutability, and exact execution boundaries could not be verified.

No protocol, retention, or authorization details were provided for chat history or cloud audit log access, which limits confidence for information disclosure and tampering coverage outside the core repudiation finding.
